transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah… I guess I’m here because I’ve been really stuck on how my face looks, especially in photos. Like there’s this one part that looks uneven to me, and now that I’m more in front of people at work—events and conventions and stuff—I keep noticing it.

Other people say they can barely see anything, but I’ll stare at pictures for way too long and it’s kind of all I can focus on. I know that probably sounds small, but it’s been bothering me a lot.
Do you find yourself avoiding social situations or events because you feel self-conscious about your appearance?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t always totally skip the events, because planning them is literally my job, but I’ll kind of get stuck before them. Like with the event materials, there were photos and staff stuff, and I spent so long worrying about how I looked in them that I missed part of a planning deadline.

And then even normal things, like vendor calls or getting ready for meetings, take way longer than they should because I’m checking or fixing things or just… distracted by it. I’ll be trying to prep an agenda and somehow end up looking at the same picture again, which is embarrassing to admit.
How much time would you say you spend each day thinking about how your face looks, especially the part you feel is uneven?

It’s… kind of hard to put an exact number on it. I mean, it started more when I had to be in front of people more at work, like photos and event stuff, and then I just kept noticing this one uneven part of my face.

Some days it feels like it’s on and off all day, especially if I see a picture of myself. I’ll tell myself I’m just checking it quickly, but then I’m staring at it way longer than I meant to. And people will say they barely notice anything, which should make me feel better, but it doesn’t really stop me from looking.
Has this concern about your facial appearance caused you significant distress or made it hard for you to function in your daily life, like at work or with friends?

Yeah… it has. I mean, I still do things, it’s not like I’m just hiding in my room all day, but it’s definitely messed with work. There was this planning deadline where I missed part of it because I got so caught up in how I looked in the event materials—like the photos and whatever we were using—and then I kept thinking, “Okay, I’ll fix this later,” but I didn’t.

And now even vendor calls or just prepping for meetings takes me longer than it should, because I’ll get distracted by checking how I look or worrying about it. It’s frustrating because the actual work isn’t even that hard sometimes, but my brain just goes off on this whole thing.
Have you ever tried to cover up or hide the part of your face that you’re concerned about, like with makeup, clothing, or posture?

Yeah, I guess I do, though it’s not always like… hiding with a scarf or anything. It’s more that before I send event pictures or join a vendor meeting, I’ll open my phone camera and check my face over and over.

Sometimes I retake photos a bunch, or I’ll tilt my head a certain way so that side doesn’t look so obvious. And then I end up asking a coworker, like, “Do I look weird?” which is awkward, because they’re trying to talk about the schedule or the vendor list and I’m stuck on my face.

It can eat up a lot of time, honestly. Like enough that I fall behind on planning stuff, and then I’m stressed about that too.
Do you think the uneven part of your face is something that others would notice, or do you feel like it’s something only you can really see?

I mean… I feel like they should notice it, because to me it’s right there, especially in photos. Like once I see it, I can’t stop staring at that one uneven-looking part of my face.

But everyone keeps saying they barely see anything, or they’ll be like, “No, you look fine,” and then they move on to talking about the event setup or whatever. I know they’re probably not spending time analyzing my face, but ever since I’ve had to be more in front of people at work, I just can’t let it go. It feels obvious to me, even if other people say it isn’t.
Do you believe that the uneven part of your face is a real physical defect, or do you sometimes think that it might be more in your head even though it still bothers you?

I mean… I don’t know. Part of me feels like it has to be real, because when I look at photos it’s like my eye goes straight to that uneven part and I can’t unsee it. Especially now that I’m more in front of people at work, it just feels really obvious to me.

But then everyone else says they barely notice anything, so then I start thinking maybe it’s more in my head than I want to admit. Like, I came in because I just can’t stop staring at it, and it’s exhausting. Even if other people don’t see it, it still bothers me a lot.
Do you worry about other parts of your body, or is your main concern focused on your face?

It’s mostly my face. I mean, I might have normal little moments where I don’t like an outfit or something, especially if I’m at a venue and everyone’s dressed up, but that’s not really what I came in for.

It’s this one uneven-looking part of my face. Ever since I’ve had to be more in front of people at work, and there are photos from events or meetings, I just keep staring at it in pictures. Even when people say they barely see anything, I still get stuck on it.
Do you find yourself doing things like checking your reflection, taking multiple photos, or asking others about your appearance because you feel so anxious about how your face looks?

Yeah… I do. Probably more than I want to admit.

Like before I send event pictures to anyone, or if I’m about to hop into a vendor meeting, I’ll open my phone camera and check my face, and then I end up checking it again because the lighting in those conference rooms is so bad—like the hotel ballroom lighting, it makes everyone look kind of strange, but I still think it’s just me.

And with photos, I’ll retake them a bunch of times or tilt my head a certain way so that uneven part doesn’t show as much. Sometimes I’ll ask a coworker, “Do I look weird?” or “Is my face doing that thing?” and they’ll usually say no, but then I don’t really believe it.

It can take up time, honestly. Like I’ll mean to be working on the planning checklist or sending something to a vendor, and then I realize I’ve spent way too long messing with my camera or the picture.
Have you ever felt like your concern about your face is so intense that it feels like something is wrong with you physically, even when others say you look normal?

Yeah… I guess it does feel that intense sometimes. Like, I came in because ever since work started putting me more in front of people, I can’t stop noticing this one uneven-looking part of my face, especially in photos.

And then everyone else is like, “I barely see anything,” but I’ll still zoom in or stare at it and think, no, something is off. It’s weird because I know lighting and angles can be awful—like at event spaces, the pictures always look strange anyway—but I still end up feeling like it’s my face specifically, like something is physically wrong with it.
Is your anxiety about your appearance specifically tied to the belief that there's something physically wrong or defective about your face, even if others don’t see it that way?

Yeah… I think that’s what it is. It’s like I can’t just see it as a bad photo or weird lighting, even though I know those meeting rooms and event spaces have the worst lighting.

I came in because once I started being in front of people more at work, I just got stuck on this one uneven-looking part of my face. Like in photos especially, I’ll stare at it and stare at it, and everyone says they barely notice anything, but to me it feels like there’s something actually wrong there.

Do you feel driven to perform certain behaviors, like checking your appearance repeatedly, changing your posture, or adjusting photos, in order to reduce the anxiety or discomfort you feel about your face?

Yeah… I do feel kind of driven to do it. Like before I send event pictures, I’ll keep opening them and zooming in, or I’ll retake them, and then I start tilting my head a certain way because I think maybe that makes the uneven part less obvious.

And before vendor meetings, I’ll check my face in my phone camera, then check again, even though I’m supposed to be looking over the agenda or the planning checklist. It’s annoying because those little checks turn into… like, a whole thing.

Sometimes I’ll ask a coworker if I look weird, too, but then I feel embarrassed because they’re busy with their own stuff, and I’m over here worrying about my face when we’re supposed to be dealing with table counts or whatever. It can eat up enough time that I fall behind on planning things.

No other ICD-10 codes are supported by the clinical presentation.

No symptoms have ruled out either condition.
